_meta.description: SEED/STARTER dataset of well-established, textbook-level drug-drug interactions, keyed by generic (INN) name pairs. This is a SMALL, deliberately conservative list of high-confidence, widely-documented interactions — it is NOT exhaustive, NOT a clinical decision support system, and MUST NOT be used as the sole basis for a clinical decision. Before any production/clinical use, this dataset should be reviewed by a qualified pharmacist/clinician and expanded against an authoritative source (e.g. a licensed drug interaction database such as DDInter, Micromedex, Lexicomp, or First Databank). Severity labels are approximate (major/moderate/minor) and mechanisms are simplified.

severityScale.major: Potentially serious or life-threatening; avoid combination or requires close monitoring/dose adjustment
severityScale.moderate: Clinically significant; monitor or adjust therapy
severityScale.minor: Usually of limited clinical significance; be aware

pairs.mechanism: Additive effect on bleeding risk (anticoagulant + antiplatelet)
pairs.recommendation: Avoid combination unless specifically indicated; monitor INR and for bleeding

pairs.mechanism: NSAID increases bleeding risk and may potentiate anticoagulant effect
pairs.recommendation: Avoid NSAIDs in patients on warfarin where possible; prefer paracetamol for pain

pairs.mechanism: Combined anticoagulant + antiplatelet effect increases bleeding risk
pairs.recommendation: Use only under specialist supervision with monitoring

pairs.mechanism: Metronidazole inhibits warfarin metabolism (CYP2C9), increasing INR/bleeding risk
pairs.recommendation: Monitor INR closely or avoid; consider alternative antibiotic

pairs.mechanism: Dual antiplatelet effect increases bleeding risk
pairs.recommendation: Often intentionally co-prescribed (e.g. post-stent) but requires monitoring for bleeding

pairs.mechanism: Ibuprofen may blunt aspirin's antiplatelet/cardioprotective effect; additive GI bleeding risk
pairs.recommendation: If both needed, space dosing and consider GI protection

pairs.mechanism: NSAIDs can reduce antihypertensive effect and impair renal function when combined with ARBs
pairs.recommendation: Monitor renal function and blood pressure; avoid prolonged NSAID use

pairs.mechanism: Same class effect as Losartan + NSAID
pairs.recommendation: Monitor renal function and blood pressure

pairs.mechanism: CYP3A4 inhibition by clarithromycin raises statin levels, increasing myopathy/rhabdomyolysis risk
pairs.recommendation: Consider temporary statin suspension during macrolide course, or use azithromycin instead

pairs.mechanism: Weaker CYP3A4 interaction than clarithromycin, but still monitored
pairs.recommendation: Generally considered safer macrolide choice; still watch for muscle symptoms

pairs.mechanism: Furosemide-induced hypokalemia increases risk of digoxin toxicity
pairs.recommendation: Monitor potassium and digoxin levels

pairs.mechanism: Macrolide inhibits digoxin clearance (P-glycoprotein), raising digoxin levels
pairs.recommendation: Monitor digoxin levels; consider alternative antibiotic

pairs.mechanism: Ciprofloxacin inhibits theophylline metabolism, risking toxicity (seizures, arrhythmia)
pairs.recommendation: Avoid combination or reduce theophylline dose with monitoring

pairs.mechanism: Alcohol increases risk of lactic acidosis with metformin
pairs.recommendation: Advise patients to avoid excess alcohol intake

pairs.mechanism: NSAIDs reduce renal clearance of methotrexate, increasing toxicity risk
pairs.recommendation: Avoid NSAIDs with methotrexate, especially at high (oncologic) doses; caution even at low weekly RA doses

pairs.mechanism: Omeprazole inhibits CYP2C19, reducing activation of clopidogrel to its active metabolite
pairs.recommendation: Prefer pantoprazole or an H2-blocker if PPI co-therapy is needed

pairs.mechanism: Weaker CYP2C19 interaction than omeprazole
pairs.recommendation: Generally preferred PPI choice alongside clopidogrel, but awareness still warranted

pairs.mechanism: Calcium binds levothyroxine in the gut, reducing absorption
pairs.recommendation: Separate dosing by at least 4 hours

pairs.mechanism: Combined potassium-sparing effect increases hyperkalemia risk
pairs.recommendation: Monitor serum potassium and renal function closely

pairs.mechanism: Same hyperkalemia mechanism as with other ARBs
pairs.recommendation: Monitor serum potassium and renal function closely

pairs.mechanism: Both increase serotonergic activity, raising risk of serotonin syndrome
pairs.recommendation: Use with caution; educate on serotonin syndrome symptoms

pairs.mechanism: Additive CNS and respiratory depression
pairs.recommendation: Avoid combination where possible; if necessary, use lowest doses with close monitoring

pairs.mechanism: Additive CNS depression from two benzodiazepines
pairs.recommendation: Avoid combining two benzodiazepines; review need for both

pairs.mechanism: Both cause vasodilation via nitric oxide pathway; combination can cause severe, life-threatening hypotension
pairs.recommendation: Contraindicated combination; do not co-administer

pairs.mechanism: Calcium chelates tetracyclines in the gut, reducing absorption
pairs.recommendation: Separate dosing by at least 2-3 hours

pairs.mechanism: Antibiotics can alter gut flora producing vitamin K, potentiating warfarin effect
pairs.recommendation: Monitor INR during and after antibiotic course
